newsitem.title: UK: UK harvest should see reasonable quality - HGCA.
newsitem.headline: UK harvest should see reasonable quality - HGCA.

text.p: Cold, wet weather in June helped alleviate the impact of earlier drought in Britain but rain may have done some damage to crops, the U.K. Home-Grown Cereals Authority said.
"It has been one of the coldest and wettest Junes this century," its Early-Summer Crop Report said.
"Although this has helped to alleviate the impact of drought in the spring, heavy rain has caused some damage and may impair quality. "
"However, crops generally remain in good condition and fine weather in the run-up to harvest should produce reasonable quality and good yielding crops."
In Scotland, the HGCA said crops are progressing well, despite heavy rain which damaged some areas. Crops just need sunshine.
In northern England, rain delayed winter barley ripening. Many crops are lodging, with the possibility of sprouting and green grain.
The HGCA said winter wheat in the North withstood the miserable weather and is progressing well, although some is beginning to go flat.

Heavy rain in the Midlands, although giving crops the boost they need, has caused lodging in some areas. In spite of the rain, a few crops on light land still show signs of drought damage, by now irreversible.
Generally, wheat crops are progressing very well, with some potentially high yields.
Considerable rainfall in the North and South of England had boosted yield prospects of winter cereals in most areas, the HGCA said. But more rain is needed on lighter soils and poorly-rooted crops.
Suprisingly, drought is still a problem in the East, despite some areas having had four to six inches of rain since early March.
Winter wheats are doing well, as is barley, which is more advanced, and has therefore been considerably less affected by the drought. But crops on light soils are still suffering.
Rapeseed crops are well advanced and Spring crops are reaching the end of their flowering. - - Louise Clemenson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
